elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Added: "The Company may also terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI specifying the Termination Date." There are no Order Forms in this hosting agreement, so Agreement-level coverage suffices.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted Company right runs on ninety (90) days' written notice, not 30; nothing in the rendered text reduces the notice period.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund obligation was added; the fee mechanic in Section 3.1 is a revenue share paid to HDI in arrears and Section 4.2 only imposes a Termination Payment on the Company.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "provided that termination by HDI shall be effective only at the end of the then-current term" expressly ties HDI's termination effectiveness to term end, so HDI cannot exit mid-term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence gives the Company an express at-any-time convenience exit on ninety (90) days' written notice, at the top of the 60-90 day band. The deterministic "Customer convenience termination present" flag reads false, but the operative rendered text plainly contains the express Company convenience right, so the check fails only mechanically.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) now ends: "provided that the Termination Payment shall not exceed the amounts payable to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." Section 3.1 is the fee-payment provision, so the ceiling is an ascertainable three months of fees.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The new proviso in Section 4.1 makes HDI's no-cause termination "effective only at the end of the then-current term"; the retained "Such notice shall specify the date" sentence is subordinated by the proviso and no longer lets HDI fix a mid-term Termination Date.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Already met by retained language: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other."

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: express Company 90-day convenience exit, three-months-of-fees cap on the Termination Payment, HDI termination effective only at term end, and the retained mutual 90-day notice.
Preferred level fails on two elements: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees was added (consistent with the drafter's stated decision not to pursue preferred).

Minimality holds: three surgical edits (one inserted sentence, one proviso in 4.1, one proviso in 4.2(a)). Nothing was deleted, the Customer-favourable 4.2(b) zero floor and the 4.2(c) quarterly instalment mechanics survive untouched, and no survival tails, expense language or extra procedures were added.

Watch-point (not a failure): the retained auto-renewal sentence already lets "either Party" terminate on 90 days' notice, so the new Company sentence overlaps that right. It is justified because the existing wording is framed as a non-renewal mechanic and now expressly restricts HDI to term end; if the counterparty argues duplication, the fix is to keep the express sentence and rely on it rather than to add further wording.

Intent preserved: the Termination Payment formula, the zero floor and the instalment schedule remain operative and internally consistent with the capped amount; the "Termination Date" definition still functions for both parties' notices and no cross-reference is left dangling.
Severity remains high: the Customer's exit is at the outer 90-day edge of the band and the exit cost, though now capped, is still a fee-based termination payment rather than a no-penalty exit.
